checks.what: qing-dynasty_1680 (1680-81) becomes Qing 1677 plus Cliopatria's Southern Ming 1677 rebel zone minus Yunnan and Taiwan. Page (Revolt of the Three Feudatories) confirms 'In 1680, the provinces of Hunan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and Sichuan were recovered by the Qing', Sichuan and southern Shaanxi 'retaken ... under Wang Jinbao and Zhao Liangdong in 1680', Kunming entered in October 1681 (Yunnan correctly left to wu-sangui-s-zhou), Zheng Keshuang surrendered October 1683 (Taiwan correctly cut). Resolved: 27209 cells against 26720 for the old correction. It adds 942 (Chongqing 307, Hubei 230, Shaanxi 132, Gansu 112, Jiangxi 102, Zhejiang 23, about 11 Laos/Vietnam border cells, 3 Hong Kong) and drops 453, of which 444 are western Sichuan (Kham) that tibet holds in the current dossiers under R2, so dropping them leaves no hole. Fujian and Guangdong stay in the shape through the Southern Ming 1677 row. Trial in my own stage: the 1680 snap goes from added 0 / removed 308 to added 631 / removed 7. Nobody's cells inside the 1677 rebel zone fall from 992 to 54 in 1680-81; the 54 left are the east coast of Taiwan, outside Tungning. Ownership from 1682 on is the same as before, because the 1682 keyframe already gives every added cell to the Qing. Tungning keeps its 101 Taiwan cells. The 1681 render shows no hole inside China. The page does not name the Hubei, Gansu, Jiangxi and Zhejiang strips. They are Cliopatria's 1677 rebel zone, the Qing hold them from the 1682 keyframe anyway, and the entry states confidence 2 for this. One small inaccuracy in why: the 1680 snap emptied only Chongqing. The other 631 cells were already nobody's on 1 Jan 1680, a hole left over from p1670-p1679, which the patch also closes.

mughal-empire_1687 (1687-90) keeps the fx-10 correction unchanged (12382 cells, identical) and adds the two dossiers' own last shapes. The bijapur-sultanate_1683 correction (828 cells) and the golconda-sultanate_1687 correction (856 cells) are cell for cell identical to the dossiers. Page (Siege of Golconda): infobox '28 January - 22 September 1687', 'Mughal Empire annexes Golconda Sultanate, Hyderabad Subah is formed', 'On 21 September 1687, a Golconda noble named Sarandaz Khan betrayed the Sultanate'; Bijapur was 'successfully besieged ... in 1685-1686' and the siege had ended by 14 January 1687. The snap runs in 1687 after that year's events (Golconda gain ledger/101), so the dating holds. Resolved: 13608 cells, 1226 more than before (Andhra 503, Karnataka 471, Telangana 207, Maharashtra 30, Tamil Nadu 10, Goa 4). In my trial 970 of them change from nobody's (published 1687-89) to Mughal. The rest were already Mughal or are kept by smaller neighbours: maratha-empire 86 (the new 57 cell-year conflict on the Kolhapur side, which the Marathas win), portuguese-india 3, coorg 2, EIC 1. The 1687 snap's removals fall from 972 to 2. The 1688 render shows the Mughal Deccan down to the Mysore and Madurai edge with no new hole. Of the added cells, 1116 are in the mughal-empire_1691 keyframe. The other 106, in central and southern Karnataka (Shimoga, Chikmagalur, Chitradurga, Tumkur) and Anantapur, have been bijapur-sultanate's in the compile since before 1670 and pass to the Mughals by Bijapur's own dissolve in 1686. The patch only keeps them Mughal through 1690; see problems. Small inaccuracy in why: the 'besieged Bijapur in 1685-1686' sentence comes from the body text, not the infobox.
